criteria.test: Is there one canonical, documented build system with a single source of truth for project metadata, usable identically across supported platforms?

Does the project run an automated test harness (e.g. ctest) integrated into the build, covering multiple explicit test categories (parser/checker, runtime smoke, stdlib/module, packaging, CLI/REPL, metadata)?
Does CI build and test on at least Linux, macOS, and Windows?
Does CI validate against more than one compiler toolchain?
Does CI run sanitizer and warnings-as-errors builds in addition to plain release builds?
Is tagging/publishing a release mechanically gated on green CI rather than a manual/ad-hoc step, with immutable tags?
Is downstream/first-party package compatibility continuously tested against core changes (cross-repo integration testing)?

metric.build_test_integration.limitations: No direct access to live CI run logs or coverage numbers was available in this packet; scoring relies on the project's own frozen release/build documentation cross-checked against externally observable release and PR history for the same repository.

quidra_score_breakdown.normalization_note: A small deduction (-6) is applied because evidence is observational (repository docs, PR/release descriptions and CI-matrix summaries) rather than a fully reproduced live CI log inspection, and because the project is a young pre-1.0 codebase with only two tagged releases observed.

Release automation is described as mechanical: the tagging workflow runs only on push to main and refuses to run twice for the same version.

criteria.test: Is there a canonical, operational (not merely descriptive) development/release/versioning workflow document?
Does the language have a complete formal/semantic specification, including a machine-checkable grammar?
Is there a complete, stable, coded reference of compiler diagnostics/runtime failures with correction guidance?
Are standard-library namespaces/APIs documented with contracts, not just examples?
Is there dedicated documentation for LLM/automation consumption and machine-discoverable schemas (patch/grammar/describe)?
Are packaging, distribution, and contribution/process concerns documented separately from the language spec?

metric.documentation_quality.limitations: Evidence is drawn from the frozen docs/ directory embedded in this task plus externally observable repository artifacts (README, PRs, releases); no independent readability/clarity NLP scoring was performed, consistent with the proxy-based rubric used here.

quidra_score_breakdown.normalization_note: A deduction (-6) reflects that documentation is concentrated in in-repo markdown/spec files rather than a generated, versioned public docs site, and that some cross-file restatement risk is only partially mitigated (README examples had to be corrected to match contracts, per observed PRs).

raw_evidence.note: Development/release doc is explicitly operational rather than descriptive, single authority for the release procedure.
raw_evidence.quote: the single authority for the release procedure

A large stable table mapping every diagnostic code to meaning and typical correction, plus a documented runtime-failure format.
